CONCERNING
EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL
The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the authority of regional governments to regulate and manage their own governmental affairs directed towards accelerating the realization of public welfare through improvement of services, Empowerment and community participation. The authority of Regional Government is to make regional policies to provide services, increase participation, initiative, and community Empowerment aimed at improving people's welfare.

The implementation of regional autonomy must always be oriented towards improving community welfare by always paying attention to the interests and aspirations that grow in society. Therefore, governmental affairs related to basic services such as basic education, health, fulfillment of minimum living needs, basic environmental infrastructure must be fulfilled.

Human rights are basic rights that are inherently attached to human beings by nature, are universal and lasting, so they must be protected, respected, maintained, and may not be ignored, reduced, or deprived by anyone. The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, specifically Article 27 paragraph (1) which states that "All citizens have equal standing before the law and government and are obliged to uphold the law and government without exception". Although the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia guarantees equality of standing for every citizen, until now women still experience various obstacles in obtaining their rights in almost all areas of life.

This has an impact, women as part of the national development process, namely as actors as well as beneficiaries of development results, have not been able to obtain optimal benefits in enjoying development results equal to men, especially in the policy formulation process and decision-making, as well as in the implementation of development in all fields and at all levels. On the other hand, women have special needs compared to men so that in accordance with their nature, in certain conditions, the Regional Government must be able to guarantee their rights are fulfilled according to those needs.

-17- Based on this, a regulation is needed that serves as a guideline for all parties, especially the Regional Government in ensuring the implementation of Empowerment and Protection of Women in Semarang City. This Regional Regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental conditions of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights in various fields of development, increase the commitment and effectiveness of regional government in implementing policies, programs and activities as well as encourage the institutional capacity of government and society that improves the quality of life of women.

Letter a Sufficiently clear.
-21- Letter b What is meant by basic rights of workers includes:
a. basic right to obtain decent wages.
b. right to obtain equal opportunity and treatment from the company without discrimination.
c. right to obtain work training to improve and develop work competence.
d. right to perform work according to the determined time.
e. right to labor placement.
f. right to obtain protection for occupational health and safety.
g. right to obtain welfare through labor social security.
h. right to participate in trade unions or labor unions.
i. right to obtain leave: at least 12 working days after the employee has worked for one year continuously.
j. right to rest: workers after working four hours continuously, obtain rest opportunity for a minimum of half an hour.
k. right to maternity leave, miscarriage and menstrual leave specifically for female workers/laborers:
Female workers/laborers are entitled to obtain rest for 1.5 (one and a half) months before the time of childbirth and 1.5 (one and a half) months after childbirth according to the calculation of an obstetrician or midwife.
Female workers/laborers who experience miscarriage are entitled to obtain rest for 1.5 (one and a half) months or in accordance with a certificate from an obstetrician or midwife.
Female workers/laborers who during menstruation feel pain and notify the employer, are not obligated to work on the first and second day during menstruation.
l. right to perform worship.
m. right to conduct work strikes.
n. right to obtain severance pay if termination of employment or dismissal occurs.
o. right to appropriate opportunity to provide breast milk to their child if this must be done during working hours.

I. GENERAL
The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the authority of regional governments to regulate and manage their own governmental affairs directed towards accelerating the realization of public welfare through improvement of services, Empowerment and community participation. The authority of Regional Government is to make regional policies to provide services, increase participation, initiative, and community Empowerment aimed at improving people's welfare.

The implementation of regional autonomy must always be oriented towards improving community welfare by always paying attention to the interests and aspirations that grow in society. Therefore, governmental affairs related to basic services such as basic education, health, fulfillment of minimum living needs, basic environmental infrastructure must be fulfilled.

Human rights are basic rights that are inherently attached to human beings by nature, are universal and lasting, so they must be protected, respected, maintained, and may not be ignored, reduced, or deprived by anyone. The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, specifically Article 27 paragraph (1) which states that "All citizens have equal standing before the law and government and are obliged to uphold the law and government without exception". Although the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia guarantees equality of standing for every citizen, until now women still experience various obstacles in obtaining their rights in almost all areas of life.

This has an impact, women as part of the national development process, namely as actors as well as beneficiaries of development results, have not been able to obtain optimal benefits in enjoying development results equal to men, especially in the policy formulation process and decision-making, as well as in the implementation of development in all fields and at all levels. On the other hand, women have special needs compared to men so that in accordance with their nature, in certain conditions, the Regional Government must be able to guarantee their rights are fulfilled according to those needs.

-17- Based on this, a regulation is needed that serves as a guideline for all parties, especially the Regional Government in ensuring the implementation of Empowerment and Protection of Women in Semarang City. This Regional Regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental conditions of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights in various fields of development, increase the commitment and effectiveness of regional government in implementing policies, programs and activities as well as encourage the institutional capacity of government and society that improves the quality of life of women.

I. GENERAL
The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the authority of regional governments to regulate and manage their own governmental affairs directed towards accelerating the realization of public welfare through improvement of services, Empowerment and community participation. The authority of Regional Government is to make regional policies to provide services, increase participation, initiative, and community Empowerment aimed at improving people's welfare.

The implementation of regional autonomy must always be oriented towards improving community welfare by always paying attention to the interests and aspirations that grow in society. Therefore, governmental affairs related to basic services such as basic education, health, fulfillment of minimum living needs, basic environmental infrastructure must be fulfilled.

Human rights are basic rights that are inherently attached to human beings by nature, are universal and lasting, so they must be protected, respected, maintained, and may not be ignored, reduced, or deprived by anyone. The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, specifically Article 27 paragraph (1) which states that "All citizens have equal standing before the law and government and are obliged to uphold the law and government without exception". Although the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia guarantees equality of standing for every citizen, until now women still experience various obstacles in obtaining their rights in almost all areas of life.

This has an impact, women as part of the national development process, namely as actors as well as beneficiaries of development results, have not been able to obtain optimal benefits in enjoying development results equal to men, especially in the policy formulation process and decision-making, as well as in the implementation of development in all fields and at all levels. On the other hand, women have special needs compared to men so that in accordance with their nature, in certain conditions, the Regional Government must be able to guarantee their rights are fulfilled according to those needs.

-17- Based on this, a regulation is needed that serves as a guideline for all parties, especially the Regional Government in ensuring the implementation of Empowerment and Protection of Women in Semarang City. This Regional Regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental conditions of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights in various fields of development, increase the commitment and effectiveness of regional government in implementing policies, programs and activities as well as encourage the institutional capacity of government and society that improves the quality of life of women.
